styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Te Papa, the cable car and the old Cuba Street quarter.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Botanic Gardens, the wild south coast and harbour views.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Coffee, craft beer and Cuba Street eating.

stays.why: Steps from the station, shops and the cable car base; easiest base without a car.
Cafés, bars and galleries on the doorstep; walk to Courtenay Place at night.
Te Papa, the harbour and the ferry terminal nearby; flat walks along the quay.
Beach and promenade views, 20–25 minutes on foot from the centre; quieter nights.

food: Order a flat white: Wellington is the self-styled coffee capital, and most cafés roast their own beans.
Eat on Cuba Street: cheap noodles, bakeries and small restaurants, roughly NZD 15–30 a main.
Try a craft beer at a Courtenay Place or Te Aro taproom; ask for a tasting paddle to sample several.
Seafood is local and good: green-lipped mussels, kaimoana and fish and chips near the waterfront.
Book dinner ahead on Friday and Saturday nights; popular small places fill up. Check opening days on the day.
more_time: Ride the ferry across the harbour to Days Bay or Eastbourne for a half-day walk and a swim in summer.
Take a bus or drive over to the Wairarapa for a day of vineyards and small towns; check timetables first.
Add a night for Zealandia wildlife sanctuary at dusk, when the native birds are most active.

recommend.why: Two nights covers Te Papa, the cable car and Botanic Gardens, plus a waterfront walk and a good meal on Cuba Street.

month_notes: January: warmest and driest, highs near 20°C; book stays early, it is peak season.
February: same warm, settled weather as January; great for the coast and harbour ferries.
March: still mild at 18°C but rain days rise to about 10; pack a light rain jacket.
April: cooler at 17°C with about 10 rain days; good for museums and café days.
May: highs drop to 15°C and rain days rise to about 12; bring layers and a windproof jacket.
June: cool at 13°C with around 12 rain days; short daylight, plan indoor sights.
July: coldest month, highs near 12°C and about 14 rain days; wettest stretch of the year.
August: still cold at 12°C with about 14 rain days; wind makes it feel colder, dress warmly.
September: slowly warming to 13°C but still about 12 rain days; expect changeable days.
October: 15°C with about 12 rain days; spring showers, keep plans flexible.
November: milder at 16°C and about 11 rain days; a good shoulder month before the crowds.
December: warming to 18°C with about 11 rain days; festive season, book ahead.

climate_guide.summary: Cool, windy maritime climate: mild summers, cool winters and rain in every month. Wind is the constant.

items.title: Best time: December to February
items.text: Warmest and driest, highs around 18–20°C with about 7 rain days a month. Best for the coast and gardens.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: Every month has rain days, peaking around 14 in July and August. Carry a small umbrella or rain jacket daily.

items.title: Windy city
items.text: Wellington is known for strong wind. A windproof layer matters more than an umbrella on exposed waterfront walks.

items.title: Cool winters (June to August)
items.text: Highs near 12–13°C and lows around 8–9°C. Bring a warm coat, especially for evening ferries and the south coast.

items.title: Mild, not hot, summers
items.text: Even in January highs stay near 20°C. Layers work better than summer beachwear for most days.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Waterproof jacket, warm mid-layer, comfortable walking shoes and sunglasses. Add a hat and sunscreen for summer.

transit.best: Walk the compact centre; use Metlink buses for hills and suburbs.

modes.text: No metro or tram in the city. Don't plan around rail inside Wellington.

Metlink buses and suburban trains cover the city. Pay with a Snapper card or contactless card. Cash fares are about $3–6 by zone; card is cheaper. Day passes cost about $13–30 by zones, after 9AM weekdays and all day weekends.
Suburban trains run under Metlink with the same Snapper or contactless payment. Useful for trips out of the centre.
Uber and DiDi work in Wellington. Taxis include Combined, Corporate, Green and Kiwi.
Handy for day trips out of the city. The compact centre is easier on foot, so pick up a car only when leaving town.
Ferries cross the harbour and to Picton. Check times on the day.

modes.text:: The Kelburn cable car climbs from Lambton Quay to the Botanic Gardens. A quick, scenic way up the hill.

modes.text: The central city is compact and best on foot. The Golden Mile links the station to Courtenay Place.
